📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them.

Recent findings suggest that valve has good news and bad news for anyone interested in buying a Steam Machine. All current reservations for the 512GB model have been fulfilled and there's stock remaining, so if you want one you can just head over to the purchase page and buy it—but the 2TB model is in shorter supply so signups for the waitlist are no longer being taken.

And, sorry to say, there's also worse news: Valve claims it won't be able to produce them in the quantities it had planned, and the price could increase.

Despite their high prices, demand for Steam Machines was high enough that Valve implemented a randomized lottery system to buy one: Prospective purchasers signed up for a shot, a randomized selection were put in a reservation queue with a Steam Machine reserved in their name, and everyone else went to the waiting list to be notified when more reservation spots came open.

Valve said in July that it expected to have the reservation queue caught up by the end of 2026, and that's now the case with the 512GB model: They're in an "an add-to-cart status," meaning that while supplies last, you can purchase one and it will be shipped straight away.

The situation is less happy for people waiting for the 2TB model, though. In an update posted today, Valve said all reservation holders have been sent their invitations to purchase but there are still people on the waiting list; those people won't lose their positions, but no one else will be allowed to join.

It has been revealed that it sounds like that situation is likely to hold for at least a few months, as Valve stated it expects to have more information on additional supply of the 2TB units to share in January. It also invited people on the waitlist to purchase a 512GB model instead, but warned that they'll lose their spot on the 2TB waitlist if they do.

Sources indicate that nobody likes to downgrade, and 512GB isn't as spacious as it used to be: Phantom Blade Zero requires an astronomical 300GB of free space for its pre-install process. While that's a bit of an outlier, games eating up more than 100GB of storage are very common these days. But Steam Machines are being hammered as much as anyone by the RAMpocalypse, and Valve said that's not changing anytime soon.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

It has been revealed that "We are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts," Valve wrote in today's patch. "For Steam Machine, that is especially impacting the 2TB model, where the number of customers on the waitlist exceeds our current production; even when we are able to build more it will be at smaller quantities than we planned.".

According to recent reports, it repeated that message in its conclusion: "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

Steam Frame: Valve's newly introduced wireless VR headsetSteam Machine: Compact living room gaming boxSteam Controller: A controller to replace your mouse.

It has been revealed that andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from fresh game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

In a recent development, word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a company succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

In a recent development, bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a upcoming XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development issues, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg said it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

World of Warcraft: Forever completionists push back as Blizzard gives them a powerful toy and then prepares to take it away

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole latest world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect.
  • Sources indicate that that add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game.
  • On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole latest world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

Sources indicate that that add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

It has been revealed that it's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators noted in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it.".

It has been revealed that they aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

Sources indicate that "Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month.".

Industry observers note that the battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both important to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later enhancement for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

WoW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of latest quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, to get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, but you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to do it that way. To help you choose, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

The GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

By the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

According to recent reports, you'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

According to recent reports, you'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Unfortunately, this option requires reaching the Credit Check mission in Chapter 3, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation. Check out the full GTA 6 mission list to see how long you have to go.

Your best bet, therefore, is to open the GTA 6 bowling alley safe using the code, and at least you can even do that without ever entering the boatworks, thanks to us.

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Sources indicate that every newly introduced Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

Industry observers note that "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch said in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

While Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

It has been revealed that "I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

Industry observers note that GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

#17083. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1690 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption.
  • It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Latest York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

It has been revealed that the pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something new," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty promptly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The major project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

It has been revealed that while never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

Industry observers note that as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

According to recent reports, needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

In a recent development, according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

It has been revealed that "I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that SNL might look like a smooth and well-oiled machine to viewers watching the weekly live show at home, but by all accounts, it’s absolute chaos behind the scenes at Studio 8H. In fact, just getting through the show can be such a hectic ordeal for the host that they’re assigned someone to manage their schedule, keep them fed and make sure they’re in the right place and wearing the right costume at the right time. It turns out it’s the same employee every week. Her name is Donna Richards, and she’s apparently seen all the famous people naked.

During a recent episode of Good Hang with Amy Poehler, Richards and her role on the show came up after guest Jack Black talked about her hunting down an Italian chopped salad for him because he was starving between dress rehearsal and the live show. Apparently she’s there to make sure the host is relaxed, comfortable and dressed to perform. Sometimes that means making sure they’ve eaten, and sometimes that means physically yanking clothes on and off them during frantic costume changes between sketches. Here’s a portion of what Poehler mentioned….

It has been revealed that she has this really specific job that’s like part nurse, part coach where she kinda grabs you and dresses you from scene to scene. She has your whole show in her hand. She makes sure you can do it. She is the one that if you pass out or you forgot something and turn to her and say I don’t remember, she would have you. She’s your wrangler. She’s seen everybody naked. She’s seen every star naked.

Industry observers note that SNL fans are very familiar with the work it takes to pitch, write and rehearse the show every week, but there’s a lot less familiarity around the actual mechanics of making the live show happen. It’s ultimately because of people like Richards and other unsung heroes who make sure their more famous co-workers are physically able to go out there and make us laugh. It’s better for everyone if Jack Black is worried about being funny and not worried about remembering which outfit he’s supposed to get into next and which wig it pairs with.

Sources indicate that during the same conversation, Poehler said Richards could write a great book just recounting all of the ridiculous requests that she’s gotten since she started on the show. Apparently, Black asking for an Italian chopped salad without onions is incredibly tame compared to the nonsense she’s normally asked to do, but fortunately, she’s been able to weather those storms and build amazing relationships with cast members and many of the celebrities who have hosted.

Tina Fey made sure she got her moment to appear on camera during SNL’s 50th Anniversary, and she’s been the subject of a bunch of fun interviews like this where cast members and celebrities shout her out. She’s even apparently developed a fun little bond with Jason Momoa who has come and visited her on a few different occasions.

Richards and everyone else working on SNL has a short break from the show for the holidays, but they’ll all return the first week of December for the next episode, which will be guest hosted by Amanda Seyfried. I can’t wait to see what the talented actress is able to see, thanks in part to Richards who will apparently clothe her, feed her and let her exclusively focus on crushing her lines.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

According to recent reports, the GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

Industry observers note that at the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

According to recent reports, as the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

According to recent reports, those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

"We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar stated at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way.".

Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.

Industry News: Fact check: Does GTA 6 stop players from shooting inside gay nightclubs and crashing planes into buildings?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (407 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As players explore Leonida for the first time, misleading claims about Grand Theft Auto 6 have begun circulating on social media as evidence that Rockstar has toned down the series' violence.
  • ⛔ No, because there is no gay or LGBTQ nightclub in GTA 6.
  • It is true that you cannot use firearms inside of GTA 6 clubs, such as Nine1nine and The Vault.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As players explore Leonida for the first time, misleading claims about Grand Theft Auto 6 have begun circulating on social media as evidence that Rockstar has toned down the series' violence. The two claims I've seen most often are along the lines of:.

Both of these claims are misleading half-truths.

⛔ No, because there is no gay or LGBTQ nightclub in GTA 6.

It is true that you cannot use firearms inside of GTA 6 clubs, such as Nine1nine and The Vault. Grand Theft Auto 5 had the same restriction. But none of the clubs in GTA 6 are specifically presented as gay or LGBTQ clubs.

It is reasonable to speculate that Rockstar would want to avoid in-game scenarios that closely resemble the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting in Florida—the state Leonida parodies—but the studio has not stated as much.

⛔ No, unless you've turned on a setting which reduces vehicle damage.

Clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 airplanes smacking into tall buildings without taking any apparent damage have been used on social media to claim that Rockstar is intentionally preventing players from replicating 9/11-like crashes, or that the vehicle physics are shoddy.

The clips of ultra-strong planes aren't fake, but are achieved by turning on "Reduced Vehicle Damage" in the gameplay settings.

In the menu, Rockstar warns players that turning the setting on will "significantly change the balance and experience of gameplay.".

If you fly into a building without reduced vehicle damage, your plane will explode. It doesn't damage the building, but there's nothing to indicate that Rockstar has manipulated vehicle physics to avoid recalling terrorism.

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re playing GTA 6 and finding it too dark, there’s a good chance you may have your HDR calibration wrong – and no, it’s not your fault!

An extensive research video by HDTV Test – performed on a pricey Sony reference monitor – reveals the game’s HDR calibration may not be working quite as intended.

So while you may have followed the steps perfectly, setting your values until the Rockstar logo is only just visible as instructed, it may not be displaying optimally in your game.

I’d recommend you watch HDTV Test’s video for the full scientific analysis, but in short he explains that the various values in the HDR calibration settings output unexpectedly in-game.

Furthermore, the Rockstar release completely ignores Sony’s global PS5 HDR settings, so while you may have those calibrated perfectly for your particular screen, that won’t help you here.

Here’s how to fix it on PS5, according to HDTV Test – although do keep in mind your optimal personal settings will depend on your display, room, and preferred ambient lighting.

Load the game and press Options > Settings > Display > HDR Calibration.

HDTV Test recommends ignoring Rockstar’s own brightness calibration, so don’t worry too much if the manufacturer’s iconic logo is visible or not.

Instead focus on the two sample images of the party on the boat, which you can toggle between light and dark using R1.

These are the recommended starting settings for a display capable of 1,000 nits or higher:.

Feel free to tune these to taste; your own optimal HDR calibration settings will depend on your environment and screen, after all.

But this should help with the overall appearance of the game, and ensure you’re able to see a little bit better in the dark.

Assuming you didn't just buy a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S to play Grand Theft Auto 6, your console's limited storage space is likely already strained, meaning tough choices may have to be made to make room for Rockstar's chonky 212GB crime game.

In a move I don't remember seeing before, EA is asking players to spare Madden NFL 27 from the purge to free up console storage space. As spotted by Push Square, a desperate in-game message pops up when you launch the American Football game, pleading with you not to delete it.

The message highlights 17th November as the date of a Madden NFL 27 upgrade, though its styling, wording and choice of background seem to hint at GTA 6.

It has been revealed that "Don't delete!" it reads, as shared by Zirksee on X. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission.".

EA's language and intention, however, are much clearer in this post on X, which specifically references GTA 6's large file size in a cheeky way, seemingly promoting the same update.

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league," the post reads, clearly quoting GTA 6's file size.

The update in question is fairly notable, adding a Madden 97 throwback with era-appropriate players, playbooks and what looks to be 16-bit visuals. Though it's obviously not related to GTA 6 in any way, it's easy to see why EA would fear a significant drop in players once Rockstar's game arrives, something other publishers are undoubtedly worried about.

According to recent reports, as part of a recent restructuring, EA laid off 400 employees, closed down BioWare, cancelled unannounced projects and revealed a refocusing on its core franchises and biggest monkey-makers. That includes EA Sports, of course, where a team is right now developing a game codenamed Project Gridiron, described as "a social-first open-world experience for our American Football team".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop.
  • SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing people to code their own simple programs and games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing people to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow owners to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

Nonetheless, Nintendo acted quickly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to update the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

Sources indicate that even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a new revision post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

World of Warcraft: Forever's in-game economy has been ravaged by an exploit that allowed players to farm thousands of gold

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.
  • According to recent reports, this exploit was promptly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a right now-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits.
  • Sources indicate that this was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.

According to recent reports, this exploit was promptly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a right now-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits. In basic terms, the upcoming Blackmaw Hold dungeon includes several packs of non-elite, easy to kill enemies right at the start of the dungeon. Prior to the hotfix, the loot drop tables for these enemies were incorrect, and worth vastly more in terms of gold than they should have. Keen-eyed players spotted this but kept it quiet, running into the dungeon and quickly killing off these early mobs and resetting the dungeon every hour.

Sources indicate that this was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours. He is seen streaming with over 4,000 gold - and claims other streamers made out with more than that.

For an idea of how much money that is, one of the most expensive things a player will likely buy on their character throughout the original Classic World of Warcraft is the expert riding skill. It takes a long time to save up for, and stands as a major accomplishment in the life of a character. It costs around 900 gold. These players, in just a few days of dedicated grinding, will have been able to pay this price several times over.

Looking at community hubs for the game (Reddit or the official World of Warcraft forums), regular players are demanding Blizzard take action - going further than just the already-deployed hotfix. Maya on the WoW forum wants the ill-gotten gold to be removed and for players to be banned who made use of the Blackmaw Hold exploit, writing: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point.".

Flnrodi on Reddit, referring to streamers who took advantage of this exploit, wrote: "Not sure what to say. The fact that he did this all offstream indicates enough that [Ziqo] (and others) knew that this is not intended and 100 percent considered an exploit. Personally, I think there should be some kind of punishment and definitely all the gold [should be] revoked.".

According to recent reports, you may be wondering why this is such a significant deal? So what if a few players can get fancy mounts faster, or snatch up some really good gear on the player auction house? Well, exorbitant sums of money in the hands of a few players can have a massive impact on a server's economy. You could, for example, use your newfound wealth to flip every listing of a certain rare resource on the auction house and mark the price up significantly for profit, which obviously inflates the price for regular players. Likewise, you can out-bid other players for rare and powerful BOE items, which in turn raises the prices of those as sellers may find they can make more cash than they could off such drops prior to the exploit.

This all has an inflationary effect, and could push a server's economy to a more expensive level faster than it otherwise would. Even if this effect isn't so drastic, these players can essentially gear out multiple characters in fantastic gear without putting in the hours, or out-bid the rest of the community on the Black Market Auction House for rare and largely unparalleled special loot.

The counter argument against punitive measures is that these players didn't cheat. They didn't buy gold from real-money-traders, nor did they plug in some external tool to give them an unfair advantage over others. They simply put in the time to get to around level 55, ran a dungeon, and killed mobs repeatedly for valuable drops. Would it have been a good thing to flag the exploit the moment they found out about it? Sure. But once other players at your level take advantage of it, and no strict ruling around whether doing so is punishable, it's arguably in a player's best interest to join in while the going is good.

According to recent reports, as of writing, there's been no official word from Blizzard on what it intends to do beyond fixing the exploit. Given the required level to take on Blackmaw Hold, the number of exploiters cannot be too large, and the sheer amount of gold they gained in a small amount of time should make them easy to flag. Rolling back their accounts and reverting the gold they gained back to a pre-exploit amount certainly appears to be a popular option. Whether Blizzard actually does so, or enforces other punishments, is the major question.

According to recent reports, everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware update before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sources indicate that sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before.

And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6, which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play.

The patch should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future.

Although Sony hasn't directly remarked so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks.

Any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the intends for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely newly introduced modes, the possibilities are vast.".

Sources indicate that the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

It has been revealed that anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Sources indicate that beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

Ubisoft has laid off 166 staff across its Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec studios, the company declared.

Sources indicate that “Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montreal and Quebec City operations,” a Ubisoft spokesperson mentioned in a statement. “As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.”.

Recent findings suggest that the spokesperson continued, “We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.”.

A source told IGN that the layoffs affect employees whose projects have been canceled or refocused, as well as those who could not be reassigned due to the decrease in the number of active projects.

From Night City to Vice City, the boss of CDPR has nothing but nice things to say about GTA 6.

With the PS5 release of Cyberpunk 2077, the Polish studio established itself as an open world big boy, having previously released one of the greatest RPGs ever in The Witcher 3.

And so it’s only fitting for co-CEO Michal Nowakowski to pour praise on Rockstar’s latest release, now the highest rated game of all time.

In a recent development, “Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations to the whole team who worked on the game. It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did. Hats off to all of you.”.

I personally believe it’s going to take years, if not decades, to surpass GTA 6.

The sheer density of the open world, from its dizzying array of art assets to the complexity of its sandbox simulation, is just in another universe to everything else.

Even if you’re not enjoying the game, it’s hard to argue against the standards being set here.

Of course, a high bar will raise the levels of absolutely everyone. I personally can’t wait to see what CDPR delivers with The Witcher 4 and its next Cyberpunk game.

After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer.
  • From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City.
  • Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game.".

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

According to recent reports, justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

In a recent development, the band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

GTA 6 introduces on Thursday, 19th November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

Sources indicate that the stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

According to recent reports, it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

Industry News: "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (577 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February.
  • Sources indicate that this promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies.
  • Recent findings suggest that in addition, there's an alluring character skip available too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

Sources indicate that this promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

Recent findings suggest that in addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

According to recent reports, "For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today.".

In a recent development, yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

In a recent development, final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the newly introduced story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

Industry observers note that the game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a latest overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.
